messages:
sara_support: FYI customer ACME reported increased tail latency (~220-380ms) and intermittent 401s since ~08:15 UTC. They say traffic from Frankfurt is hitting us-west1.
ryan_netops: Can you paste a sample request-id + client IP? Also, any DNS resolver they mentioned? @sara_support
sara_support: req id req_7f3a2c, client ip 185.62.34.11, customer says their corp resolver is doing EDNS. Ticket created by deploy-bot: INC-2481 :ticket:
deploy-bot: Created incident INC-2481 (support) — assigned to netops.
devin_sre: Quick repro: from my laptop (eu-resolver) I get A -> eu-edge.redwood.net (ip 3.122.45.10). From a public resolver (1.1.1.1) I get us-west1 (34.82.16.9). Suspect EDNS client-subnet or resolver-affinity mismatch.
ryan_netops: Paste dig outputs please (incl +edns=0). We need to see authority, TTLs, and any cdn geo answers. Also check SOA and zone config.
sara_support: here's what customer provided (redacted):
```
$ dig @10.0.0.2 api.redwood.com +short
34.82.16.9

$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.com +short
3.122.45.10

$ dig @10.0.0.2 api.redwood.com +noall +answer
api.redwood.com. 300 IN A 34.82.16.9
```

devin_sre: I ran an EDNS probe from two EU datacenters:
```
# from frankfurt resolver (gives us-west)
dig @fkt-resolver api.redwood.com +edns=0 +short -> 34.82.16.9
# from london resolver (gives eu)
dig @lon-resolver api.redwood.com +edns=0 +short -> 3.122.45.10
```
This suggests our authoritative returns different answers depending on EDNS client-subnet or resolver IP. Possible stale geoip DB on one authoritative, or upstream anycast inconsistent pop mappings.
ingrid_product: Customer also reported billing spike because client retried on 401 and got routed to other region, double counting tokens. Need urgent mitigation for billing and auth.
ryan_netops: Immediate steps: 1) Add temporary DNS TTL=60 for api.redwood.com to speed propagation. 2) Add an override in our geo-routing to prefer eu endpoints for queries originating from EU IP blocks while we investigate. 3) Ask customer to test with 1.1.1.1 and Google 8.8.8.8 and report back.
devin_sre: Root cause hypothesis: our geoip mapping table on auth-edge cluster is out of sync with authoritative DNS, causing fallback to us-west when prefix match fails. Also EDNS client-subnet exposures cause resolvers to send different subnet hints. Reproduce plan:
- run `dig +trace` from customer resolver and public resolvers
- capture tcpdump on auth-edge in eu-pop for req_7f3a2c
- compare geoip lookup vs authoritative zone mapping

ryan_netops: Can someone run tcpdump and paste first 50 lines? If we see upstream resolver EDNS option with client-subnet, that will explain divergent answers.
sara_support: ACME says they tested with 8.8.8.8 and still saw the US IP for some requests. They flushed their caches.
devin_sre: Update: found authoritative at ns1 returning inconsistent answers between two servers (ns1 and ns3). ns1 has older geoip rules. Filing PR to sync zone. Also found EDNS handling flag was accidentally turned off on ns3 causing fallback behavior.
ryan_netops: Temporary mitigation deployed: lowered TTL and forced eu-pref routing policy (will hold for 2 hours). Notified billing to freeze invoicing for retries during window.
ingrid_product: Thanks — can we add an automated alert for EDNS mismatch across authoritative servers? This caused too much customer pain.
devin_sre: Agreed. I'll add a checker that queries multiple well-known resolvers and compares answers; alert on >5% divergence.
sara_support: Customer confirmed latency back to normal after our change. They want postmortem and assurance that billing will be adjusted. Closing interim incident, leaving postmortem follow-up in INC-2481.
deploy-bot: INC-2481 moved to status: monitoring.
